events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 11 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach to the Victoria St entrance was 612 m, and the GPS track shows he was never within 200 m at any time. [F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
C2: The driver stayed stationary 613 m from the pickup from 08:13:10 until he cancelled at 08:19:30 (6 min 20 s), i.e. he waited away from the pickup point, not at it. [F2 F3] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: The platform's own timeline never recorded the driver's arrival at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), so NS-1 (ii) is not satisfied. [F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: When the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 he was 613 m from the pickup and spent 0 seconds inside 200 m afterwards; the tap therefore does not satisfy the arrival requirement of NS-1. [F5 F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: Any waiting period the driver served was served 613 m from the pickup point, not "at the pick-up location", so the >3-minute wait in NS-1 (iii) is not established either. [F2 F5] [NS-1 NS-2]
C6: Because at least one of NS-1's conditions fails, the whole $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full for this driver-cancelled no-show. [F3 F7] [NS-2 NS-0]
C7: The driver's written claim that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than three minutes is contradicted by the GPS records showing he never came within 200 m of the pickup; the system record prevails. [F13 F1 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C8: The driver's excuse of jammed traffic is unsupported: Victoria Street and North Bridge Road were both recorded at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) during 08:00–08:30, there were no incidents near the route, and the weather was fair — and in any case congestion does not permit marking arrival 613 m away. [F14 F15 F16 F17 F13] [NS-1 NS-2]
C9: The rider was at the stated meeting point the whole time, as her chat "I'm at the entrance and I don't see any car" at 08:17 is consistent with the GPS showing no driver ever arrived. [F11 F1] [NS-2]
C10: Because the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 613 m away, i.e. not at the pickup point, an account flag for abuse of the arrival/cancellation button should be attached in addition to the refund. [F5 F1] [NS-2]
C11: The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days (2 disputes, 2 upheld, both no-show), which supports the flag_account request; the rider has no disputes and a 4.9 rating. [F19 F18] [NS-2 RD-6]
Weaknesses: The driver did tap "I'm Here" and was stationary for 6 min 20 s (F5, F2), so he will argue a genuine wait occurred and that NS-1 (iii) is met on duration alone; our answer is that the duration is irrelevant because (i)/(ii) fail on location (F1, F4). | The driver's statement and chat "I'm here already" (F10, F13) give a superficial account of arrival, and the chat requests are not tagged as threats or admissions; we rely on the GPS/timeline records overriding them (F1, F4, F5). | There is a small internal tension in the timeline: one fact says the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 (F5) while another says he never tapped it (F6); the favourable reading of F6 cannot be pressed hard, so we rest the case on F1, F4 and F5. | No toll or ERP overcharge issue exists here (F7, F8), so the only recoverable sum is the $6.61 cancellation fee; a judge could view the dispute as low-value. | The rider's own messages do not show her sending a plate request answered by the driver (F11), so the other side may argue she made no further effort to locate the car despite being told to come out (F10).
Asks: refund_full $6.61

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach to the Victoria St entrance was 612 m, and the GPS track shows he was never within 200 m at any time.
The driver stayed stationary 613 m from the pickup from 08:13:10 until he cancelled at 08:19:30 (6 min 20 s), i.e. he waited away from the pickup point, not at it.
The platform's own timeline never recorded the driver's arrival at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), so NS-1 (ii) is not satisfied.
When the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 he was 613 m from the pickup and spent 0 seconds inside 200 m afterwards; the tap therefore does not satisfy the arrival requirement of NS-1.
Any waiting period the driver served was served 613 m from the pickup point, not "at the pick-up location", so the >3-minute wait in NS-1 (iii) is not established either.
Because at least one of NS-1's conditions fails, the whole $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full for this driver-cancelled no-show.

The driver's written claim that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than three minutes is contradicted by the GPS records showing he never came within 200 m of the pickup; the system record prevails.

The driver's excuse of jammed traffic is unsupported: Victoria Street and North Bridge Road were both recorded at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) during 08:00–08:30, there were no incidents near the route, and the weather was fair — and in any case congestion does not permit marking arrival 613 m away.
The rider was at the stated meeting point the whole time, as her chat "I'm at the entrance and I don't see any car" at 08:17 is consistent with the GPS showing no driver ever arrived.

Because the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 613 m away, i.e. not at the pickup point, an account flag for abuse of the arrival/cancellation button should be attached in addition to the refund.
The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days (2 disputes, 2 upheld, both no-show), which supports the flag_account request; the rider has no disputes and a 4.9 rating.

weaknesses: The driver did tap "I'm Here" and was stationary for 6 min 20 s (F5, F2), so he will argue a genuine wait occurred and that NS-1 (iii) is met on duration alone; our answer is that the duration is irrelevant because (i)/(ii) fail on location (F1, F4).

The driver's statement and chat "I'm here already" (F10, F13) give a superficial account of arrival, and the chat requests are not tagged as threats or admissions; we rely on the GPS/timeline records overriding them (F1, F4, F5).

There is a small internal tension in the timeline: one fact says the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 (F5) while another says he never tapped it (F6); the favourable reading of F6 cannot be pressed hard, so we rest the case on F1, F4 and F5.
No toll or ERP overcharge issue exists here (F7, F8), so the only recoverable sum is the $6.61 cancellation fee; a judge could view the dispute as low-value.

The rider's own messages do not show her sending a plate request answered by the driver (F11), so the other side may argue she made no further effort to locate the car despite being told to come out (F10).

events.title: Driver Advocate brief: 10 claims (0 void)
events.body:
D1: The no-show fee turns on NS-1: the driver must have tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him within the pickup radius and must have waited inside that radius for more than 3 minutes; the system records show he satisfied neither the location nor the in-radius waiting element. [F1 F2 F5] [NS-1]
D2: The driver's closest approach to the Victoria St entrance was 612 m at 08:15:30 and he never entered the 200 m pickup radius at any point, so NS-1(ii) fails on the GPS record. [F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
D3: He tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while 613 m from the pickup point and accumulated 0 seconds within 200 m after the tap, so NS-1(iii) (over 3 minutes of waiting at the pickup point) also fails. [F5 F2] [NS-1 NS-2]
D4: The driver was stationary 08:13:10–08:19:30 at a point 613 m from the pickup, which matches the rider's account and the chat sequence during which the rider was at the entrance asking where the car was; a stationary 6 min 20 s hold 613 m away is not waiting "at the pick-up point". [F2 F9 F11 F10] [NS-1]
D5: The driver's own written statement that he waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (613 m away, 0 s inside 200 m), so under the system-records-win rule that statement cannot establish NS-1. [F13 F1 F5] [NS-1 NS-2]
D6: His explanation that Victoria Street was too jammed to get closer is not corroborated: the traffic records show Victoria Street and North Bridge Road at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) with no incidents near the route during the trip window, and fair weather, so there is no traffic fact excusing the 613 m gap. [F14 F15 F16 F17 F13] [NS-1 NS-2]
D7: The platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at null) and the tap-time record shows no "I'm Here" at all in that record set, consistent with a 613 m approach that never met the arrival condition. [F4 F6 F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
D8: Because the driver cancelled as a no-show without meeting NS-1, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full; the fee on record is $6.61 with no surge applied. [F3 F7 F8] [NS-2 NS-0]
D9: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius (within_200m false), which is the abuse-of-the-arrival-button pattern that attracts the additional account-review referral under NS-2. [F5 F1] [NS-2]
D10: The driver's 90-day record already shows 2 disputes, both upheld and both no-show disputes, so this second non-compliant no-show cancellation supports the account-review referral as a repeat pattern. [F19] [NS-2]
Weaknesses: The rider's own fare and cancellation records (F3, F7) show the $6.61 fee was actually charged, and the driver's chat message (F12) shows he did wait from 08:13 to 08:19 in some form, which could be argued as a good-faith attempt rather than abuse. | The driver asserts the rider never appeared (F13) and the rider's chat (F11) does not prove the rider was standing at the exact Victoria St entrance; the rider's presence rests on the rider's own messages (F9, F11) rather than an independent system record. | The two inconsistent timeline entries on the "I'm Here" tap (F5 gives 08:16:00 at 613 m while F6 says no tap was recorded) give the other side room to argue the arrival-button record is unreliable, though on either reading NS-1(ii)/(iii) still fail. | The 200 m pickup radius is a data-layer parameter (policy gap G2), not an official Ryde figure, so the driver could argue the "at the pick-up location" distance is not authoritatively fixed at 200 m.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

He tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while 613 m from the pickup point and accumulated 0 seconds within 200 m after the tap, so NS-1(iii) (over 3 minutes of waiting at the pickup point) also fails.

The driver was stationary 08:13:10–08:19:30 at a point 613 m from the pickup, which matches the rider's account and the chat sequence during which the rider was at the entrance asking where the car was; a stationary 6 min 20 s hold 613 m away is not waiting "at the pick-up point".

The driver's own written statement that he waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (613 m away, 0 s inside 200 m), so under the system-records-win rule that statement cannot establish NS-1.

His explanation that Victoria Street was too jammed to get closer is not corroborated: the traffic records show Victoria Street and North Bridge Road at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) with no incidents near the route during the trip window, and fair weather, so there is no traffic fact excusing the 613 m gap.

The platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at null) and the tap-time record shows no "I'm Here" at all in that record set, consistent with a 613 m approach that never met the arrival condition.

The driver asserts the rider never appeared (F13) and the rider's chat (F11) does not prove the rider was standing at the exact Victoria St entrance; the rider's presence rests on the rider's own messages (F9, F11) rather than an independent system record.

The two inconsistent timeline entries on the "I'm Here" tap (F5 gives 08:16:00 at 613 m while F6 says no tap was recorded) give the other side room to argue the arrival-button record is unreliable, though on either reading NS-1(ii)/(iii) still fail.

On (ii), the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 612 m at 08:15:30 and he was never inside the 200 m arrival radius at any time [F1]; at the moment of the tap he was 613 m from the pickup [F5]. claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach to the Victoria St entrance was 612 m, and the GPS track shows he was never within 200 m at any time.
The driver stayed stationary 613 m from the pickup from 08:13:10 until he cancelled at 08:19:30 (6 min 20 s), i.e. he waited away from the pickup point, not at it.
The platform's own timeline never recorded the driver's arrival at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), so NS-1 (ii) is not satisfied.
When the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 he was 613 m from the pickup and spent 0 seconds inside 200 m afterwards; the tap therefore does not satisfy the arrival requirement of NS-1.
Any waiting period the driver served was served 613 m from the pickup point, not "at the pick-up location", so the >3-minute wait in NS-1 (iii) is not established either.
Because at least one of NS-1's conditions fails, the whole $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full for this driver-cancelled no-show.

The driver's written claim that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than three minutes is contradicted by the GPS records showing he never came within 200 m of the pickup; the system record prevails.

The driver's excuse of jammed traffic is unsupported: Victoria Street and North Bridge Road were both recorded at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) during 08:00–08:30, there were no incidents near the route, and the weather was fair — and in any case congestion does not permit marking arrival 613 m away.
The rider was at the stated meeting point the whole time, as her chat "I'm at the entrance and I don't see any car" at 08:17 is consistent with the GPS showing no driver ever arrived.

Because the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 613 m away, i.e. not at the pickup point, an account flag for abuse of the arrival/cancellation button should be attached in addition to the refund.

The driver's statement and chat "I'm here already" (F10, F13) give a superficial account of arrival, and the chat requests are not tagged as threats or admissions; we rely on the GPS/timeline records overriding them (F1, F4, F5).

There is a small internal tension in the timeline: one fact says the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 (F5) while another says he never tapped it (F6); the favourable reading of F6 cannot be pressed hard, so we rest the case on F1, F4 and F5.
No toll or ERP overcharge issue exists here (F7, F8), so the only recoverable sum is the $6.61 cancellation fee; a judge could view the dispute as low-value.

The driver's closest approach to the Victoria St entrance was 612 m at 08:15:30 and he never entered the 200 m pickup radius at any point, so NS-1(ii) fails on the GPS record.
He tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while 613 m from the pickup point and accumulated 0 seconds within 200 m after the tap, so NS-1(iii) (over 3 minutes of waiting at the pickup point) also fails.

The driver was stationary 08:13:10–08:19:30 at a point 613 m from the pickup, which matches the rider's account and the chat sequence during which the rider was at the entrance asking where the car was; a stationary 6 min 20 s hold 613 m away is not waiting "at the pick-up point".

The driver's own written statement that he waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (613 m away, 0 s inside 200 m), so under the system-records-win rule that statement cannot establish NS-1.

His explanation that Victoria Street was too jammed to get closer is not corroborated: the traffic records show Victoria Street and North Bridge Road at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) with no incidents near the route during the trip window, and fair weather, so there is no traffic fact excusing the 613 m gap.

The platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at null) and the tap-time record shows no "I'm Here" at all in that record set, consistent with a 613 m approach that never met the arrival condition.
Because the driver cancelled as a no-show without meeting NS-1, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full; the fee on record is $6.61 with no surge applied.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius (within_200m false), which is the abuse-of-the-arrival-button pattern that attracts the additional account-review referral under NS-2.
The driver's 90-day record already shows 2 disputes, both upheld and both no-show disputes, so this second non-compliant no-show cancellation supports the account-review referral as a repeat pattern.

weaknesses: The rider's own fare and cancellation records (F3, F7) show the $6.61 fee was actually charged, and the driver's chat message (F12) shows he did wait from 08:13 to 08:19 in some form, which could be argued as a good-faith attempt rather than abuse.

The driver asserts the rider never appeared (F13) and the rider's chat (F11) does not prove the rider was standing at the exact Victoria St entrance; the rider's presence rests on the rider's own messages (F9, F11) rather than an independent system record.

The two inconsistent timeline entries on the "I'm Here" tap (F5 gives 08:16:00 at 613 m while F6 says no tap was recorded) give the other side room to argue the arrival-button record is unreliable, though on either reading NS-1(ii)/(iii) still fail.
The 200 m pickup radius is a data-layer parameter (policy gap G2), not an official Ryde figure, so the driver could argue the "at the pick-up location" distance is not authoritatively fixed at 200 m.

points.response: Agreed and adopted: NS-1 fails for the driver on both the location and the in-radius waiting element, which is exactly why the fee must be reversed under NS-2.

Adopted — and it goes further than the driver admits: the closest approach of 612 m at 08:15:30 means he never came within the radius at any moment, so NS-1(ii) fails outright and the fee is refundable in full under NS-2.

Adopted, with one correction in the rider's favour: the tap at 08:16:00 was made 613 m out with 0 s inside the radius afterwards (F5), so it is the abuse pattern, not a mere shortfall — the full $6.61 is refundable under NS-2.

Adopted: a 6 min 20 s stationary hold at 613 m (F2) is not waiting "at the pick-up point", and the rider's messages show she was at the entrance asking where the car was (F9, F11, F10) — the fee is refundable under NS-1 read with NS-2.

Adopted: the driver's statement of a 3-minute wait at the pickup is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records showing 613 m out and 0 s inside 200 m (F13 vs F1, F5), so it cannot establish NS-1 and the refund follows under NS-2.

Adopted: band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Victoria Street and North Bridge Road with no incidents near the route and fair weather (F14–F17) leaves the 613 m gap unexplained, and congestion could not in any event license pressing "I'm Here" from 613 m away.
Adopted: with driver_arrived_at null (F4) and no in-radius track (F1), the platform never recorded an arrival, so NS-1 fails; I do not rely on F6 and prefer the more specific tap-time record.
Adopted in full: the $6.61 fee on record with no surge (F3, F7, F8) must be refunded in full under NS-2, which is the rider's requested outcome.
Adopted and I keep the account-review referral: a tap at 08:16:00 while GPS put him outside the radius (F5, F1) is the abuse-of-the-arrival-button pattern NS-2 attaches to the refund.

Adopted: the driver's 90-day record of 2 disputes, both upheld and both no-show (F19), supports the repeat-pattern basis for the account-review referral under NS-2, alongside his 4.6 rating versus the rider's clean record (F18).
My C3 stands and is reinforced rather than withdrawn: the null driver_arrived_at (F4) is a system record, and the driver's side does not contest it — it confirms NS-1's location element fails.
My C4 is unchanged: the 08:16:00 tap at 613 m with 0 s inside 200 m (F5) is the factual core of the refund, and the driver's own brief now accepts the same reading.
My C10 (account referral) is only strengthened by the driver's concession on the tap location and by his 2-of-2 upheld no-show history (F5, F1, F19).

Conceded — we do not contest the GPS geometry: the closest approach was 612 m and the driver was never inside 200 m (F1, F5), so on the face of the record NS-1(ii) fails and the fee cannot stand; our client's position is that this is a genuine operational miss, not a fabricated arrival.

The rider is right that the 6 min 20 s stationary period was 613 m from the pickup (F2, F3); we only note for the record that this is the conduct the driver described as a wait, which bears on whether NS-2's abuse referral is the right characterisation rather than on whether the fee is refundable.
Conceded — driver_arrived_at is null, so no arrival was recorded and NS-1(ii) is not met on the platform record; we do not ask the judge to treat the driver's late tap as an arrival.

We do not dispute that the tap occurred 613 m out with 0 s subsequently inside 200 m (F5, F1); this satisfies the account-review limb of NS-2, which is exactly the added action our own brief already accepts at D9.

Duration is not the deciding element once NS-1(i)/(ii) fail on the GPS record (F1, F5), so we agree the >3-minute wait cannot rescue the fee; our client's mitigation is only that the wait was real in duration (F2, F12), which goes to character not to liability.
Agreed in principle: with NS-1 failing, NS-2 requires the $6.61 on record (F3, F7) to be refunded in full, which is the outcome our own brief requests.
Conceded — the system records win over the driver's written statement (F13 contradicted by F1 and F4), and our brief D5 already accepts that point against our own client.

Conceded on the traffic evidence: band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Victoria Street and North Bridge Road with no incidents and fair weather (F14, F15, F16, F17) does not corroborate the driver's congestion excuse, and no clause permits marking arrival 613 m away on that basis.

We do not contest that the rider reported being at the entrance at 08:17 (F11) and that no driver arrival is recorded (F1); we note only that the rider's presence is established by her own messages rather than an independent system record, which neither strengthens nor defeats the NS-2 refund.

Conceded — the tap at 613 m with 0 s inside 200 m (F5, F1) triggers the additional account-review referral under NS-2, and our brief D9/D10 already asks for it; the refund and the flag are not alternatives.

Conceded as to the profile facts (F19; rider F18): the two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days support the NS-2 referral, though we note profile facts may only support the added action and not decide the fee outcome, and RD-6 is a route-deviation clause with no application to this no-show case.

We narrow our own D10: the account-review referral rests on the NS-2 abuse limb (F5, F1) and the 90-day no-show history (F19); the rider's clean record (F18) is not in issue and we withdraw any reliance on RD-6, which governs route deviation and cannot be cited for a no-show.
